cost.note: The topic is named and one real charge is quantified, but no amount a citizen pays for this service is given. The corporation states a 'Nil' transaction fee for online payment, which is an explicit zero on the channel charge and is retained here under protocol section 3 so that the cell is not scored absent. It is not the amount the citizen pays: the tax itself cannot be derived from any public page, because the corporation's own method points to a percentage table 'given above' and to an annexure of location-wise basic rates, neither of which is on the page, which ends with the text 'TO BE UPDATED'; the calculator that would supply them points at an unreachable staging host. That gap is carried as a separate unknown claim rather than folded into this cell. Under the section 8 cost definition the payment route is a payment step without an amount, which is mentioned.

documents.note: The topic is named without an actionable value for this scenario. The only instrument the payment route names is a cheque or demand draft drawn in a particular favour, which is a payment method rather than a document the citizen must produce. The corporation does publish a real document list on the same page, comprising registered documents, a filled Form-6 and the last tax paid receipt, but it is given for applying for assessment, which this scope excludes, and it is not counted here.

eligibility.note: Usable rules decide which route applies: the citizen must have the property tax bill number, given as a zone number, division code, bill number and sub number, and is told to confirm it before paying; the payment may be made through tax collectors, eleven named banks, e-seva centres or online; and the liability is a half-yearly tax on a property inside Chennai city limits.

time.note: The topic is named without an actionable value. The tax is described as half-yearly, which tells the citizen there is a cycle but not when a half year's tax falls due; no reviewed route gives a due date, a penalty date, a rebate deadline or a service-level target for the payment route. The timelines the corporation does publish belong to the assessment procedure, which this scope excludes.

owner.note: The citizen can identify and reach the role that holds the case: the Revenue Officer, Corporation of Chennai, named as the payee for a cheque or demand draft on one route and, on the payment and receipt routes themselves, as the officer to whom a discrepancy in the property tax should be taken, with two telephone numbers and an extension published beside the form.

after-submission.note: A visible post-payment surface exists and is public: a Property Tax Online Payment Receipt route that returns a receipt for a property identified by its four-part bill number, without login, alongside published payment-status routes. The routes were read, not exercised; no identifier was entered and no case data was retrieved, which is why the receipt claim is recorded as mixed and partial rather than as a verified observation of what it returns.
